questions.question: Hardly had we reached the school _______.
questions.explanation: Scarcely/Hardly + had + V3 + **when** + Past Indefinite. → "Hardly had we reached the school when the bell rang."

questions.question: As soon as I came in, she ______ the room.
questions.explanation: Two past actions joined by "As soon as" → both use Past Indefinite. → "As soon as I came in, she left the room."

questions.question: My mother ______ suffering from fever since Friday.
questions.explanation: Future action continuing from a point in time → Future Perfect Continuous: will have been + V-ing. → "will have been suffering."

questions.question: Just now he_________ his dinner but he says he will see you when he's finished.
questions.explanation: "Just now," "yet," "already," "recently" → Present Perfect tense. "have" + past participle "had" → "has had."

questions.question: The teacher failed to make the students ______ to him.
questions.explanation: Causative verb "make" + object → base form of verb (no "to"). → "make the students listen."

questions.question: The rest of the page __ illegible.
questions.explanation: "The rest of the page" treated as a single collective unit → singular verb. → "is illegible."

questions.question: My brother could not help but ______ at his condition.
questions.explanation: "Cannot/could not help but" → base form of verb. "Can't help" → verb + ing. "Can't but" → base form. → "could not help but cry."

questions.question: Arafat's behavior is worthy of ________ by the youngers.
questions.explanation: After preposition "of" → verb + ing. The question tests both vocabulary (emulation/following) and grammar. "Following" fits contextually here.

questions.question: The path ______ paved, so we were able to walk through the path.
questions.explanation: Two past clauses: earlier completed action → Past Perfect. "The path had been paved" (earlier) + "we were able to walk" (later).

questions.question: He talked as though he ______ the matter.
questions.explanation: Past Simple + "as though/as if" → Past Perfect. → "He talked as though he had known the matter."

questions.question: I had Sumi ______ from the class for her reckless activities.
questions.explanation: Causative "had/have" + animate object (Sumi) → base form. → "had Sumi expel." (Inanimate object → past participle: "had my car washed.")

questions.question: Masum will get an electrician ______ the heating.
questions.explanation: Causative "get" + animate object → infinitive (to + verb). → "get an electrician to mend." (Inanimate object → past participle: "get the house painted.")

questions.question: Which one is not correct?

options.a: Majority are present in this meeting.
options.c: Only a small minority of students is opposed to the scheme.
options.d:
Majority is present in this meeting.
**

questions.correct_answer_text: Majority are present in this meeting.
questions.explanation: "Majority" alone (without "of") → singular verb. "Majority of + plural noun" → plural verb. Option A should be "Majority is present."

questions.question: Fill in the blank: I couldn't mend the computer myself, so I ___ at a shop.
questions.explanation: Causative "had" + inanimate object (it/computer) → past participle. → "had it mended at a shop."

questions.question: I was accustomed to ___ long hours to meet project deadlines.
questions.explanation: After "accustomed to," "used to" (adjective sense), "look forward to," "with a view to," "worth" → verb + ing. → "accustomed to working."

questions.question: If it rains, ___.

options.d:
the ground will have been wet
**

questions.explanation: Zero conditional (universal truth): if + Present Simple → Present Simple. → "If it rains, the ground gets wet."

questions.question: Let's arrange a party in case ___.
questions.explanation: "In case" → always followed by Present Indefinite (for future reference). → "in case Dipa comes."

questions.question: Coffee and tea ___ now-a-days offered as alternative.
questions.explanation: Two distinct items joined by "and" → plural verb. Coffee and tea are separate things → "are offered."

questions.question: Which sentence is the correct one?

options.a: I wish I were a bird!
options.b: I wish I have been a bird.
options.c: I wish I was a bird.
options.d:
I wish I were a bird.
**

questions.correct_answer_text: I wish I were a bird.
questions.explanation: Optative/wish sentence expressing unreal wish → subjunctive "were" (not "was"). "I wish I were a bird." (without exclamation mark — pure optative form).

questions.question: If I ___ enough riches, I would have established a school for street children.
questions.explanation: Third conditional (unreal past): If + Past Perfect → would have + V3. "If I had had enough riches" — first "had" = Past Perfect auxiliary, second "had" = past participle of "have."

questions.question: Fill in the gap: If these criminals ___, it would have created mass dissatisfaction.
questions.explanation: Third conditional + Passive: main clause has "would have" → if-clause needs Past Perfect Passive. "criminals" is semantic object acting as subject → "had been forgiven."

questions.question: Fill in the gap: She kept utterly silent as if the dead man ___ to her.
questions.explanation: Main clause = Past Indefinite → "as if" clause = Past Perfect. "The dead man" = semantic object acting as subject → Passive. → "had not been known."

questions.question: The scientist attempted to ___ the error before publishing.
questions.explanation: "Rectify" means to put right or correct an error. The scientist wanted to fix/correct the error before publishing.

questions.question: Would that he could _____ my feelings better.
questions.explanation: 'Would that' introduces an unreal wish, followed by Subject + could + base form of verb. So 'could understand' is correct.

questions.question: You need not _____ about the test; everything will be fine.
questions.explanation: When 'need' is used as a modal auxiliary in negative sentences, it takes 'not' + bare infinitive. 'Need not worry' is correct.

questions.question: They ___ be waiting for you at the station now.
questions.explanation: To express present possibility/speculation, 'may' is used: Subject + may + be + V-ing. 'May be waiting' expresses that it is possible they are waiting.

questions.question: It is high time _____ your heart.
questions.explanation: 'It is high time' without a following subject takes 'to + base verb'. The correct form is 'to follow'.

questions.question: I got my brother _______ paint the wall.
questions.explanation: With causative verb 'get': get + object + to + infinitive. 'Make/let/have' use bare infinitive, but 'get' requires 'to + infinitive'.
